newsitem.title: UK: Dollar inches up vs yen, mark but knocked by stg.
newsitem.headline: Dollar inches up vs yen, mark but knocked by stg.

text.p: The dollar inched back up against the yen and the mark at midsession on Thursday, recovering from an early retracement from Wednesday's strong tone.
But it slid against sterling as British Chancellor Gordon Brown's insistence he would not try to talk down the strong pound boosted the British unit across the board.
Dealers said they saw the dollar staying within ranges all day, as the currency markets had a listless feel and lacked direction in the wake of peaks earlier in the week.
"The dollar's basically rangetrading across the board," said Bobby Jasper, trader at Fuji Bank in London.
"The market had got a bit long and it needed to retract a bit," said Jasper.

At 1045 GMT, the dollar had climbed back to 118.29/39 yen after earlier slipping more than a yen from Wednesday's 11-week high of 118.95. Dealers said the dollar found resistance at Tuesday's high at 118.45. Dollar/mark was at 1.8331/36, steady from late Wednesday, having broken through resistance at 1.8270.

However, the dollar eased against sterling, whose recovery was aided by comments by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, who said he had no plans for a special autumn budget to brake consumer spending.
